paper: P. K. A. Wai, C. R. Menyuk, H. H. Chen, Stability of solitons in randomly varying birefringent fibers, Opt. Lett. 16, 1231 (1991)
description: Randomly rotating birefringence sections (paper Eq. (2)) over the coupled NLSE with deterministic walk-off delta (paper Eq. (1)); reproduction of (i) the first-order soliton shadow after one soliton period (analytic Eqs. (5)/(6) vs numerics), (ii) the delay identity delay = delta * integral cos(2 theta) dxi over 40 soliton periods, (iii) bounded pulse-width statistics for delta = 1.25..7.5, (iv) the polarization budget (locked for delta <= 1.3, depolarized but bounded for large delta).

model.rotation_law: per section of length z_h: U' = cos(theta) U + sin(theta) exp(i phi) V; V' = -sin(theta) exp(-i phi) U + cos(theta) V (paper Eq. (2)); theta, phi uniform on [0, 2*pi)
model.walkoff_local: paper Eq. (1): each axis drifts delta*t0 per unit xi = delta*|beta2|/t0 per meter (relative 2*delta*|beta2|/t0); engine walkoff (relative, local y channel) = 2*delta*|beta2|/t0, split symmetrically +-walkoff/2 about the mean frame
model.normalized_distance: xi = |beta2| z / t0^2; one soliton period z0 = pi t0^2 / (2|beta2|) corresponds to dxi = pi/2. Confirmed by the paper's own variance formula (p. 1233): Var[int cos(2 theta) dxi] = pi^2 z_h Z / (8 z0^2), which the discrete random walk reproduces exactly for dxi = (pi/2) z_h/z0 per section
model.fwm_terms: dropped by the paper (R delta >> 1: 'rapidly varying, will average to zero'); engine coupling='incoherent' (SPM + 2/3 XPM)
model.averaged_limit: 8/9 Manakov (paper Eq. (3)); launch soliton = Manakov soliton with the full power in the U direction (chi = 0)
model.launch: U = sqrt(9/8 * P1) sech(t/T0), V = 0 (paper Eq. (6): U(0) = sqrt(9/8) A sech(A(t - delta*I)), A = 1)

paper_numbers.note_z0: soliton period of the 50-ps (intensity FWHM) solitons; z_h = 100 m = z0/550 (Fig. 1 caption: axes rotate every z0/500, Sec. III uses z_h = 100 m with z0 = 55 km)
paper_numbers.R_delta_condition: R delta equals 4*(soliton period)/(beat length), large in practice -> FWM dropped
paper_numbers.seeds_note: paper Figs. 1-4 all use ONE particular theta/phi sequence; five different random sequences per delta were tried and 'qualitatively similar'

numerics.runtime_note: 40 z0 = 2200 km at 100 m sections = 22000 split steps per delta; one fixed theta/phi sequence shared across the five delta values (paper's protocol)
